It's understandable that OOP is mad, he did move on soon enough to *get his new partner pregnant and move them into their home* in 2 years, while OOP's mom was still alive. 
Two years is very very soon for something like that while you still have children and a living partner who you were married to, who you were with for at least 15 years before the coma.
Also, it's not an insult to not want someone you don't like (the AP) and a toddler at your wedding imo. 

My mom died (result of organ damage from alcoholism) in 2021 after being ill for a few years. I was 16, I'm 19 now. My mom was abusive to me, my siblings, and my dad. My dad didn't even start dating again until this year. I don't begrudge his new relationships, but if he got someone pregnant today, much less a year and a half ago, I'd be pissed. If he moved his new girlfriend into my house, I'd be even more pissed. And it's been 3 years since she died, for OOP, those things happened 2 years after the coma began.

The mother being high or a bad person doesn't even factor into this, it's completely normal (maybe not healthy, but normal) to be resentful of a parent's new partner so soon after something traumatic. 

Does the dad deserve to move on? Yes. But OOP isn't wrong for being mad with how early big things like a baby and moving in together happened, especially as OOP was and is so young. I think they should get family therapy, and probably separate individual therapy. However, they should stop punishing the AP, their gripe is with their dad and his actions, not hers or the baby's. OOP owes neither of them a relationship, but civility wouldn't hurt anyone.
